explanation: Glass is an amorphous solid, and at room temperature it would take far longer than the age of the universe to sag visibly. Old panes were simply uneven when made.

claims.text: Old windows are not thicker at the bottom because glass flows; window glass does not flow measurably at room temperature over centuries.
At room temperature, visible sagging of window glass would take far longer than the age of the universe.
Old window panes were uneven in thickness when they were made.

evidence.restatement: Window glass is far too viscous at room temperature to flow measurably in centuries; uneven old panes come from how crown and cylinder glass was made, and glaziers did not always fit the thick edge at the bottom.

Published estimates from the room-temperature viscosity of window glass put any visible sagging at vastly longer than the age of the universe, about 13.8 billion years.

evidence.restatement: Pre-modern panes, crown and early cylinder glass, were uneven in thickness when they were made.
Window glass does not flow measurably at room temperature. Old panes are uneven because crown and cylinder glass-making produced uneven sheets, and glaziers often set the thicker edge down.
